scope: NCollection_Array1/Array2 SetValue(const T&) and Init(const T&) for copy-assignment-only element types
integration_status: committed candidate; root integration and cleanup pending

candidate_bindings.domain: Initialized owned or exclusive borrowed target storage, an external or disjoint shared donor and explicit copy-assignment operation, including types with no Clone/copy constructor. Defined callback failure state and native flat-order Init semantics.

changes: Add four const-donor SetValue and Init assignment policies without Clone or Default requirements.
Generalize the private assignment helper so mutable- and const-donor SetValue operations share validation and callback invocation without constructing or destroying element objects.
Route the four existing Clone convenience methods through the same policies using T::clone_from; no Clone constructor or extra detachment is introduced for owned or mutable borrowed storage.
Preserve native partial target state after early/late assignment failure. Init visits the inherited flat range in order and stops at the failing callback.
Verify Array2 Init traverses the actual inherited Array1 length, including zero or lengths smaller/larger than its unchanged rectangular dimensions.
probe_policy: The native payload deletes its copy constructor and exposes only const-reference copy assignment. Rust omits Clone and injects an Rc trace recorder. Q events record every assignment and X events record destruction. Owned and borrowed fixtures observe caller donor destruction after the call; disjoint same-allocation donors stay unchanged. Eleven tests consume all 58 native rows; two additional tests compile non-Default/non-Clone payloads with FnOnce SetValue and stateful FnMut Init callbacks.
limitations: Native const assignment and overload selection are represented by explicit Rust callbacks. The existing Clone convenience methods continue requiring Clone, while the new methods support assignment-only types.

Donor and target must have compatible disjoint Rust borrows. Native self assignment, a donor aliasing a target within the initialized range, arbitrary overlapping wrappers and raw const-cast writable aliases remain open.

Shared read-only views retain their existing detachment-on-mutation behavior; this does not claim equivalence to native writable const-reference buffer aliases. Native supported owned/exclusive-borrowed storage receives no extra detachment.

Array2 SetValue accesses Data after rectangle validation; shortened inherited backing storage can make native access undefined. Rust checked rejection receives no native parity credit. Array2 Init uses its actual inherited length and remains defined for the observed mismatched shapes.

Rust panic/native exception comparisons cover assignment order, target/donor state and defined destruction events. Callback reentry, retained raw aliases, throwing destructors, allocation policy and uninitialized storage are not claimed.

Existing mutable-donor and original test behavior remains covered by cumulative regressions and strict Miri. No original assertions, global inventory, or legacy mapping declarations are changed; both array classes remain incomplete.
